summary: Dorchester County tower financed by West Virginia Pulp and Paper; a 1969-70 state report links it to the 1929 start of private-land detection and says it was in year-round service. No later source found.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower, first for private land in the state (1969-70 report)

events.note: Year the 1969-70 state report gives for the start of private-land fire detection; the report does not state a construction date for this tower
Described as still in year-round service under a cooperative agreement (report period July 1969 to June 1970)

evidence.supports: The tower was financed by West Virginia Pulp and Paper Company and sits near Summerville in Dorchester County
evidence.quote: This tower, financed by West Virginia Pulp and Paper Company, is located near Summerville in Dorchester County

evidence.supports: The tower was first known as the Middleton Gardens tower
evidence.quote: was originally known as the Middleton Gardens tower

evidence.supports: The report dates the real beginning of private-land fire detection to 1929

evidence.quote: Mr. C.P. Cuthbert, who was employed by West Virginia Pulp and Paper Company, supervised the erection of the first steel forest fire lookout tower for private lands in the state

evidence.quote: This is generally regarded as the first fire tower constructed in South Carolina

(Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/69 to 6/30/70)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1969-70 report calls the Summerville tower generally regarded as the first fire tower built in the state. The Commission dates its own first tower to August 1930 near Camden. Both can hold: if the Summerville tower dates to 1929 as the report implies, it predates the Commission's first and was a private-land tower.

notes_for_editor: The 1929 date and the company's role rest on one source, the 1969-70 state report as transcribed on the Eastern US Lookouts page. A 2000 Greenville News article gives 1928 for the company's first tower, but it returned 403 and was seen only as a search snippet, so it is not used. The wncfirepics Tower 302 photos are a town fire department tower, not this lookout. No source describes the site after 1970.
